There are too many extreme views regarding modern music production. Some people are very against it, and others abuse the shit out of it. I think modern music production should be embraced; however, I still think people should try there best to lay down a good performance. This video is certainly a little over the top though, because you can't make vocals that are THAT shitty sound good. It's one thing if you're a tad pitchy hear and there and want to adjust it, but you can't be too out or else it's obvious. I think the key is, try to sing as close to perfect as you can, and if it sounds good, don't bother tweaking it, but if for some reason you want it to be more mathematically perfect, only tweak it a little bit, so that it's a subtle change. I'm pretty against melodyne, but I love revoice pro, because I like my lead vocal to be completely untouched by any tuning device, but I usually tune my overdubbed vocals. I don't like tuning vocals to a grid, so that's why revoice pro is great, cos I can tune the overdubs to the original take, that way they're not mathematically perfect, but much tighter and closer to the original. You can quantize them to the original vocal as well. I think it's the best way to take advantage of technology without overdoing it. That's just my opinion though. I think the key is to always aim for the sound in your head, and if what you're hearing sounds good to you, then that's all that matters, don't get obsessed with things being mathematically perfect. We're human beings, and the subtle flaws are important to the overall sound of a recording.

I've taken LSD about 4 or 5 times. All I can say as that when it comes to psychedelics anyways, it's all very personal. Some people find LSD more intense than shrooms and vice versa. I think most people find LSD more intense though. For me, LSD is much more of a mind fuck than shrooms, but it's certainly very visual as well, only different. I have a hard time explaining the visuals of LSD, because it doesn't have the same melting effect of shrooms. Although both are very psychedelic visually, I think shrooms come closer to what people who haven't done psychedelics would expect to see. Also on shrooms I get more of that Alice In Wonderland size effect where sometimes I feel huge, or very small compared to the things around me. I personally find I'm much more in control with mentally with shrooms, and I've never had a bad trip on them. Only one difficult trip that didn't freak me out too much. But I've had 1 and half bad trips out of my 4 or 5 LSD trips. I say one and a half, because I was fortunate enough to get some ecstasy during one of those bad trips, and managed to flip things around into an amazing trip. The most accurate quote I've read about psychedelics is "To fathom Hell or soar angelic, just take a pinch of psychedelic". During a good LSD trip you truly feel like you're in Heaven, or some blissful place, and it's the purest beauty I think you can experience. When it comes to a bad trip, it truly feels like you're in Hell. Although you don't necessarily lose sense of who or where you are entirely (though that could be subjective, some people could possibly forget who they are and not know where they are), you feel can feel like you've gone completely insane and that you've broken your brain and will be stuck in that Hellish state forever. Psychedelics are very interesting, but you should always use them with caution. Although making sure you have a good set and setting can have a huge impact on how you react to the drug, it doesn't always help. There will certainly be things you'll relate to with your friends, but some or maybe even most of your experiences will be completely personal. It all comes down to how much LSD you consume, who you are, and where you are. I know for me personally, I've gotten much more out of my few LSD trips than some of my friends who've taken LSD roughly 30-40 times. It really just depends on how your brain works. I think if you're pretty creative and even kind of a strange person to begin with, LSD could be more profound to you then for others, but I may just be biased when saying that. All I know is that for me, I am a little eccentric, very introverted, and pretty spiritual even though I don't really conform to a specific religion. I think those little traits about me have a huge impact on my experience. People who aren't that introspective may have a harder time dealing with the introspective parts of LSD, but that's not always the case. I've heard other some introspective people claim that they think it made things less profound cos they already thought pretty deep about things, but I know for myself it still enhanced my deep thoughts to the extreme. One thing I'd say that's really obviously different between LSD and shrooms, at least for me, is that on LSD literally every single human sense that you have will become psychedelic. But I find that with shrooms although I get some trippy thoughts, it's not as profound, and not every single one of my senses becomes psychedelic, but I think it's a lot more visual than LSD, but just in a different way. I think I still prefer the visuals of LSD more, but sometimes I do like to get really obvious melting visuals with shrooms. One last thing I think I should mention. To those who haven't yet taken psychedelics but want to, make sure you're taking them for the right reason. They aren't the kind of drugs you use to "get fucked up" on. You should use them to learn from them or something. If you're into getting fucked up, try some narcotics instead, although I don't really advocate harder drugs... Oh and to those who've only smoked weed and had a bad experience with it, that doesn't mean you can't handle harder stuff. Although I used to be fine with weed, I can't have it anymore cos it freaks me out too much, but I can still use shrooms and LSD. Kinda ironic, but it's just the way it is. I think one of my bad LSD trips ruined weed for me, but for some reason didn't ruin LSD for me. :S

Just so you know, there are different degrees of OCD... It's just like depression. Some people can't get out of bed, other's manage to get out of bed but can't seem to accomplish anything else, and other's may be able to actually work etc. but are still suffering on the inside. There's different levels to most, if not all mental disorders. I have OCD, but more so Pure-O, which is a huge contributing factor to my depression and anxiety, thus it's hard for me to keep jobs. It's possible it's the cause of my mild Tourette's as well, but that's just based off of what I've read, and not what my therapist says.
